caption: The drawing depicts an early bicycle, also known as a velocipede, illustrated in detail with two views: a side view in the center-left and a front view in the upper-right. The bicycle has two large wheels of equal size with many evenly spaced spokes, all rendered in shades of brown and grey. The frame appears metallic, drawn in dark grey and black tones, with the connections and joints clearly shown. The handlebars are straight and capped at each end, colored brown to match the seat and pedal ends. The seat is depicted as a simple, narrow saddle, also in brown. The pedals are positioned midway along the frame, situated on either side of the central axis. The background of the drawing is plain and off-white, with minimal shading, and the artist’s name “Alfred C. Koehn” is noted in small text towards the lower left corner.
title: Bicycle
